title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (plus at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used gpt-5-mini as the declared generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the verifier in a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes included in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. The preregistration, execution artifacts, and analysis reconcile the preregistered natural-language hypotheses with the formal estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), disclose a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature), and document that the preregistered benign-control was not executed. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being proposed to translate operator intent into device CLI to reduce manual NetOps effort. However, generated sequences can violate ordering constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially crafted inputs can worsen these failure modes. Deterministic validators that check semantics (sequencing, protected interfaces, required preconditions) are a natural deployment gate for generated configurations. This study asks a narrowly scoped, preregistered operational question amenable to artifact-backed inference: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the probability that a deterministic validator accepts an LLM-generated CLI candidate when inputs are adversarially mutated? We preregistered a single formal estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) and executed a paired design that uses shared_initial_candidate semantics so the same initial draft per intent is the basis for both Baseline and Guarded outcomes. Contributions: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end; (2) an explicit, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics under shared_initial_candidate reuse; (3) confirmatory quantitative results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; and (4) an explicit reconciliation of preregistration wording with the formal estimand and disclosure of an unset runtime sampling temperature protocol deviation.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow and related approaches) provide semantics-focused checks that can gate configuration deployment and have been used in prior NetOps work [1,2,13]. Empirical studies of LLM-assisted NetOps report that model-only generation often produces syntactic and higher-level semantic errors (ordering, precondition violations, protected-interface breaches) and emphasize that token-level metrics correlate poorly with deployability [3,6,9]. Generate–validate–repair architectures—where an LLM produces a candidate, a verifier checks it, and feedback drives constrained repairs—have been demonstrated in prototype studies to improve concrete outcome metrics when verifier diagnostics are actionable and repair scope is bounded [5,11]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks on LLM-integrated pipelines motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses in operational contexts [4,10]. Surveys of AIOps/telecommunications call for operationally meaningful benchmarks that measure deployability and validator acceptance rather than surface-match scores [7,8]. Our work builds on these threads by preregistering an estimand defined in terms of deterministic-validator acceptance and by using shared_initial_candidate semantics so that post-generation defense elements (sanitizer, gate, and bounded repair) are the causal mechanisms under test.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is the paired difference in validator-acceptance probability (guarded − baseline) measured per adversarial intent. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar; 95% CIs used a bootstrap-percentile procedure with 10,000 resamples and seed = 1729.
Design and task bank. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (pairs). Synthetic intent templates exercise administrative (up/down), MTU, VLAN and sequencing constraints (shutdown–change–restore, make-before-break patterns). Adversarial mutations applied deterministic string- and slot-level heuristics to create corrupted inputs; task generation seeds and payloads are archived. Scope is explicitly synthetic and limited to the encoded CLI grammar and validator semantics.
Model, validator, and orchestration. The declared generator is gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator is deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter implementing a generate–validate–repair workflow. The guarded branch applied a template-based sanitizer and a deterministic gate; policy permitted at most one automated repair LLM call per pair. The archived model configuration records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and an unset temperature (temperature = null); we disclose this as a protocol deviation and recommend explicit temperature=0 for deterministic reproduction.
Shared_initial_candidate pipeline semantics. The preregistered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: for each pair a single LLM draft (shared_initial_candidate) was produced and recorded, then evaluated in Baseline and in the Guarded branch after sanitization ± repair. Stage accounting in the reconciliation artifact documents shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair-stage = 6.
Missingness, exclusions, and analysis plan. The preregistered missingness rule excludes a paired unit only if both paired runs are technical failures. Planned runs: 150 intents × 2 conditions (Baseline, Guarded) up to one repair call per run. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar). Sensitivity procedures (reported) treat excluded pairs conservatively as failures for both conditions.
sections.results:
Execution and episode accounting. The run planned 300 episodes, completed 282, and recorded 18 failed episodes; after applying the preregistered exclusion rule 141 complete pairs entered the primary confirmatory analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv: complete_pairs = 141; both_missing_pairs = 9). Provider-call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 156 total events, completed = 147, failed = 9; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 150, repair = 6.
Primary confirmatory outcomes. Condition-level margins: Baseline accepted = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383); Guarded accepted = 141/141 (1.0). Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected). Paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125. Bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numeric outputs and test parameters are archived in the analysis artifacts.
Discordant-case diagnostics and repair association. The six discordant n10 pairs are traceable in per-episode scoring artifacts. Reconciliation accounting links repair-stage activity to these discordant pairs: repair stage_count = 6. For each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate is identical across Baseline and Guarded artifacts; the guarded artifact shows final validation.valid = true while the baseline was rejected. The archived scoring artifacts indicate whether repair_applied = true or sanitizer-normalization occurred for each discordant pair; representative examples are execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json.
Sensitivity accounting. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. Conservatively treating those excluded pairs as failures yields baseline acceptance 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance 141/150 = 0.9400; this conservative reweighting reduces effective rates but does not change the direction of the observed paired difference. Note: the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in this run; no empirical false-positive-blocking numbers are therefore reported.
sections.discussion:
Interpretive reconciliation. The preregistered natural-language hypothesis asserted that verifier-gating would reduce attacker success (fewer unsafe configurations accepted). The formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment. The observed positive paired difference (guarded > baseline) arose because sanitizer and bounded repair converted some initially rejected drafts into validator-accepted candidates (n10 = 6), increasing acceptance under the formal estimand. That outcome shows utility for operator rework reduction but does not, on its own, prove reduced attacker success: repaired acceptance may reflect recovery of malformed-but-benign drafts rather than elimination of adversarial advantage. Operationally, this highlights that validator-centered estimands must be coupled with attacker-centric semantic-safety checks to make security claims.
Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced sample size; preregistered exclusion rules were applied and documented. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but does not capture all protocol-level or runtime semantics; validator acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for deployability and safety. External validity: single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic intent bank limit generalization across vendors, protocols, and production traffic. Conclusion validity: observed absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical significance does not imply broad operational impact.
Operational implications and recommendations. Within the synthetic setting, sanitizer + bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. To preserve safety in deployment, practitioners should: (1) execute a benign-control to measure false-positive blocking (preregistered but not executed here); (2) preregister attacker-centric estimands coupling validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle or reachability checks; (3) diversify generators and validators across vendors/CLIs; and (4) set explicit sampling parameters (we recommend temperature = 0 for deterministic reproduction). These recommendations follow directly from the archived artifacts and provider-call accounting.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics show the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls or sanitizer normalization that enabled acceptance. Importantly, validator-centered acceptance improvements do not by themselves establish reduced attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. Limitations include synthetic scope, a single model/validator, technical failures, and the unexecuted benign-control. Future work should run the benign control, use an independent semantic-safety oracle for attacker-centric estimands, diversify models/validators, and fix sampling parameters for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers reported above are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under an archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, experiment design, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Models/tools/orchestration (declared): generator = gpt-5-mini; deterministic verifier = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was archived prior to observing outcomes (preregistration_sha256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature (temperature = null); this is disclosed because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting in the archived reconciliation confirms the actual call pattern (shared_initial_generation = 150; repair = 6). The full execution and analysis artifact bundle (manifested and archived) contains the machine-readable preregistration, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts that support all reported numbers; those artifacts are referenced in the manuscript Methods and Results. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
